posts.title: California, Explained: LCFF, the formula that pays for your schools.
posts.caption: California, Explained: LCFF, the formula that pays for your schools. Since 2013, California has funded schools with the Local Control Funding Formula. Every district gets a base amount for every student, and then extra money follows the students who need more support: English learners, foster youth, and students from low-income families. The neediest districts get more still. And every district must write a public plan, the LCAP, showing how that money follows the students it is meant for. The formula is the promise. The plan is the receipt. Read the plan, and see whether the money went where the law said it should. California, Explained. Follow @davidsicairos_ and get the full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: Who watches the county government when nobody is watching? In Merced County, the answer is nineteen
posts.caption:
Who watches the county government when nobody is watching? In Merced County, the answer is nineteen ordinary citizens. The civil grand jury serves a one-year term starting January first, and the foreperson is appointed by the grand jury judge. They split into committees and investigate county departments, cities, and special districts. Any citizen can file a complaint, and that complaint can trigger an investigation. Twice a year they publish reports with findings and recommendations, and the agencies they investigate have to answer in writing. It is the one watchdog in county government that answers to no politician, only to the California Constitution. California, Explained.

posts.title: The district attorney is the one county office that decides who faces criminal charges.
posts.caption:
The district attorney is the one county office that decides who faces criminal charges. The DA is elected, not hired, and that changes everything. The board of supervisors sets the budget, but they cannot fire the DA. Only the voters can. The DA decides which cases to file, which to decline, and what charges fit the evidence. That decision shapes bail, plea offers, trials, and sentences. In a county like Merced, that means the cases that touch every family. The job is political whether the DA likes it or not, because the voters decide it every four years. So when you vote for DA, you are not just picking a prosecutor. You are picking the person who decides what justice looks like in your county. California, Explained.

Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: The board sets the direction, but one person runs the county day to day.
posts.caption: The board sets the direction, but one person runs the county day to day. The county administrative officer, the CAO, is the board's hire, not an elected official. The CAO turns the budget the board adopts into actual work: departments, contracts, hiring, and the daily decisions that keep the county moving. The CAO recommends the budget, then carries it out once the board votes. Department heads report to the CAO, and the CAO reports to the board. That chain matters, because when a county service fails, the question is not just who voted, it is who managed. The CAO is where the board's promises meet the county's payroll. So when you watch a board meeting, watch for the CAO's report, because that is where you learn what the county is actually doing. California, Explained. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: Five People Run Your County
posts.caption: Five people run your county. The board of supervisors is the county's elected governing body, five members, one per district, four-year terms. They adopt the county budget, and that budget pays for the sheriff, the district attorney, public health, roads, and elections. They hire the county administrator, who runs the day-to-day work. They approve contracts, set county policy, and hear land-use appeals. And they meet in public, because the Brown Act says your local government does its business where you can see it. So when something in the county feels off, start at the board table, because five seats, one for your district, are filled by your vote. California, Explained.
